dedupe_keys.name: rainwater saving and use in households bremen climate adapt case study

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes how Bremen reduces the load on its sewer system by getting households to keep and use rainwater. Since court rulings, and by law since 2010, the rainwater fee is separate from the wastewater fee and based on sealed property area, at 0.63 euros per m2 a year; it is refunded for water that is infiltrated or used instead of discharged. The Federal State of Bremen subsidises rainwater cisterns for toilets and gardens with up to 12,000 euros, at most a third of costs that start at about 6,000 euros, under a scheme begun in the 1990s and renewed in 2016. Coverage is the city of Bremen. The page is accessible online as free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal, published in 2018 and updated in 2026. Caveats: the page gives no measured reduction in sewer flows, not every system saves the owner money, and there was no stakeholder participation in the design. Simulation uses: fee and subsidy levers for runoff reduction in drainage and sewer capacity scenarios. Related records: the Lappeenranta stormwater case study (case_study-lappeenranta-stormwater-management-lake-saimaa).
name: Rainwater saving and use in households, Bremen (Climate-ADAPT case study)
outcomes: Subsidies and fee refunds were the main reason households adopted rainwater cisterns, which take roof water off the public sewer.
